description: Healthy baseline, then telemetry stops arriving entirely for two windows (as if the client process restarted, per PRD Journey C), then resumes at the same healthy rate.

timeline.note: client process killed mid-send, per PRD Journey C step 1; zero samples arrive for this window
client still restarting/re-registering; second consecutive empty window
client reconnected with a fresh session identity per Journey C step 2; telemetry resumes at the same healthy rate

expectedStates.reason: window 60-70s had zero samples (< minSamplesPerWindow): insufficient data, not evidence of congestion
window 70-80s also empty; still insufficient data
telemetry resumed in 80-90s with a healthy, sufficient-sample window; the baseline formed before the gap is still within baselineWindowSeconds (60s old) and is reused rather than re-formed from zero

notes: This fixture encodes a deliberate ASSUMPTION flagged in Docs/detector-test-scenarios.md: that recovery from a session gap reuses the still-recent pre-gap baseline rather than requiring a full fresh baselineWindowSeconds of new data, and that a single sufficient-sample window is enough to confirm 'healthy' after a gap (lighter-weight than the degrade/recover hysteresis counters, since this transition is about data sufficiency, not inflation hysteresis). PP-005 should treat this as a design question to confirm, not as a settled contract — if the chosen design instead re-forms the baseline from scratch after any gap, update the expectedStates at t=90 accordingly and say so in the detector's own documentation. Either way, the gap itself must produce unknown, never degraded: a missing client is not evidence of congestion.
